name: Learn a few magic tricks well enough to perform
blurb: The difference between knowing a trick and performing one is scripting, misdirection and the confidence to hold a room. Three polished tricks beat thirty half-learned ones.
gear: A deck of cards, coins, a rubber band or two
steps: Choose three tricks with different methods so no one can find a pattern.
Learn each method until your hands do it without thought — the method must be invisible even to you.
Write a script: what you say, where you pause, what you do while their attention is elsewhere.
Rehearse misdirection deliberately: the secret move happens during a laugh, a question, or a look away.
Perform in the mirror, then to a camera, then to one friend, then to strangers.
Build the set so the strongest trick is last, and learn to stop when you are ahead.
tips: Never announce what will happen in advance — it lets them watch for it.
Never repeat a trick, and never explain the method.
If a move fails, carry on. Most audiences do not know what was supposed to happen.
proof: You perform a three-trick set for strangers, with a script, and nobody works out how any of it was done.
